text.tspan: Lifecycle rule example (filter by prefix, tags or object size)
• Transition actions: move objects to another class (e.g. Standard-IA 60 days after creation, Glacier for archiving after 6 months).
• Expiration actions: delete after a time (e.g. access log files after 365 days), plus old versions (noncurrent) and incomplete multipart uploads.
• Rules can target a prefix, object tags, or object size. Since Jul 2026 objects can move to Standard-IA / One Zone-IA from day 0
(the old 30-day wait is gone). Objects under 128 KB don't transition by default.
S3 Intelligent-Tiering: moves each object by its own access pattern
• Small monthly monitoring and auto-tiering fee per object · NO retrieval charges · no minimum storage duration.
• Accessing an object in an infrequent / archive-instant tier moves it back to Frequent Access automatically.
• Archive Access (3-5 h) and Deep Archive Access (within 12 h) must be switched on (opt-in) and need a restore.
• Your notes said "700+ days": the docs give a maximum of 730 days for both optional tiers.
• Objects under 128 KB are not monitored and always stay in Frequent Access (no monitoring fee).
